reasoning_steps: Rearrange x = 1/y into xy = 1.
Incorrectly treat a product of two first-degree variables as a first-degree expression.
Choose x = 1/y as a straight line.
Try to clear denominators in x/y = y/2 by multiplying both sides by 2y.
Drop one factor of y and mistakenly write 2x = y instead of 2x = y^2.
Conclude from the incorrectly simplified equation that the first option is a line.
Misread the superscript −2 in x^(−2) as subtraction of 2.
Interpret the option as x−2+y = 1.
Rearrange that different equation into x+y = 3 and select the second option.
Omit the leading 1 and treat the equation as tan^2(theta) = 4.
Take the positive square root to get tan(theta) = 2.
Report arctan(2), approximately 63.435 degrees, instead of checking the original equation.
Attempt to subtract 1 from both sides.
Calculate 4−1 as 1 rather than 3.
Use tan^2(theta) = 1 and select the listed angle 45 degrees.
Misread tan as cot in the displayed equation.
Solve 1+cot^2(theta) = 4, so cot(theta) = √3 for the listed acute angles.
Select 30 degrees, which solves the altered equation.
Incorrectly assume the angles are in the same ratio as the side lengths.
Calculate the largest angle as 180 × 3/(1+2√2+3), approximately 79.08 degrees.
Choose the nearest listed value, 80 degrees, even though the side-to-angle proportionality assumption is invalid.
Try to apply the cosine rule to the angle opposite the side of relative length 3.
Miscalculate (2√2)^2 as 4 rather than 8.
Report 135 degrees from that incorrectly computed cosine.
Correctly recognise a right triangle with hypotenuse 3k.
Find the angle opposite the smallest side k rather than the largest side.
Report arcsin(1/3), approximately 19.47 degrees, instead of the right angle.
